summary: Reduce new-block observation latency and bound synchronization work during Bitcoin RPC pressure
details: Default BH and indexer idle observation to 250 milliseconds, independently collect Bitcoin and BH status, and wake indexer synchronization when relevant upstream state changes. Explicit polling configuration remains authoritative.

Apply bounded runtime retries to transient read-only Bitcoin RPC failures and capped exponential service backoff. Preserve cancellation, canonical hash checks and completed database commits; native bootstrap retains its separate retry policy.

Default BH batch_mode to adaptive: start at up to 32 blocks, halve on RPC retries or slow successful batches down to min(16, batch_size), and grow after four full fast retry-free commits without exceeding batch_size. The existing default cap remains 128 and explicit smaller caps remain effective.

Select the native block payload source and refresh its local index once per batch. Stop requesting the range suffix after a failed or cancelled RPC read while retaining linkage and final canonicality checks before atomic commit.
operator_actions: Upgrade the node kit and matching usdb-services image through the normal release procedure, retaining existing Bitcoin, BH, indexer and chain data. Updating only the node kit does not install the new Rust runtime behavior.

To preserve an exact fixed batch upper bound or run a comparison, set BH_SYNC_BATCH_MODE=fixed and retain the desired BH_SYNC_BATCH_SIZE in node.env. Otherwise the new adaptive default applies; a cap of 16 remains 16.
